unit.text:
- **Trạng thái:** Settled (Request-to-Run P2 Runnable Plans hoàn tất, 2026-10-01)
- **Bối cảnh:** Trước P2, việc phân rã và chọn capability/cơ chế bị phân mảnh bởi lớp prose L2 DemandFacts (8 fields) -> matcher -> `form` (`inline|protocol|facade`). Các facade `fgos-code-change`, `fgos-code-panel`, `fgos-plan-loop` tự lập lịch, tự chạy vòng lặp bằng prose, tạo ra nhiều sequencer chồng chéo và gắn chặt vào domain coding.
- **Quyết định:**
  1. **Unit là hợp đồng dữ liệu duy nhất (`src/runner/execution/unit.mjs`):** Mọi đường vào (prompt tự do, plan AgentKit, phase file) đều quy về Unit. `fgos plan-lint` kiểm chứng Unit trong phase file (`## Units`, `- unit:`), phát hiện sớm ghim hạ tầng (G2), trùng id, vòng phụ thuộc, và giao nhau `writes` không có `dependsOn`.
  2. **Driver mỏng (`core/skills/fgos-run`):** Thay thế toàn bộ các facade cũ (`fgos-code-change`, `fgos-code-panel`, `fgos-plan-loop`, `fgos-capability-dispatching`). Driver không tự lập lịch, không tự merge mà giao trọn cho **Workflow runner** (`src/workflow/runner.mjs`, P3a).
  3. **Cổng người thống nhất:** Authorize không parse từ prose plan. Phase chưa được duyệt sẽ dừng ở cổng người của Workflow run (`gate: { kind: "human" }`), owner trả lời qua `fgos workflow answer`. Mọi câu hỏi treo được gom thành một bộ duy nhất.
  4. **Xoá bỏ DemandFacts & matcher:** Xoá `src/runner/capability-match.mjs`, verb `fgos capability match`, các fragment `capability-matching.md`. L2 chỉ còn hiểu yêu cầu và viết Unit với `capability` (`domain:verb`).
Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.

Cổng nào chủ động khai `mode: "input"` thì câu trả lời nội dung là đủ để tiến bước.
  4. **Xoá bỏ DemandFacts & matcher:** Xoá `src/runner/capability-match.mjs`, verb `fgos capability match`, các fragment `capability-matching.md`. L2 chỉ còn hiểu yêu cầu và viết Unit với `capability` (`domain:verb`).

unit.sample:

- **Bối cảnh:** Sau 0047, `bind().transport`, `resolvePosture` và `nextCandidate` tồn tại nhưng không
ancestry: Lịch sử quyết định retired từ docs/decisions/ (tsk-1lv-4)
0050 — P6 Nối thật: herdr là transport mặc định, posture một đường, fallback quota qua pane mới
unit.text:
- **Trạng thái:** Settled cho ca 1, 2, 3, 4, 6; ca 5 NOT RUN (xem bằng chứng)
- **Bối cảnh:** Sau 0047, `bind().transport`, `resolvePosture` và `nextCandidate` tồn tại nhưng không ai gọi: mọi lần chạy thật là cli headless, posture tự dựng `bwrapArgs` riêng song song với driver confinement, `canApplyPosture` luôn `true`.
- **Quyết định:**
  1. **Transport do `bind()` quyết, `run.mjs` đọc.** herdr khi herdr có mặt trong session **và** executor có invocation `herdr-spawn` có id mà `canApplyPosture` chấp nhận; ngược lại cli (lý do ghi ở `provenance.transport.source`). Transport và invocation thật nằm trong `assignment.json` / `unit.json`, không chỉ ở giá trị trả về. Executor có CLI vẫn out-of-process (D-ADR0033 (một cơ chế dispatch, executor có CLI luôn chạy ngoài process)).
  2. **Posture một đường.** `resolvePosture` chỉ ánh xạ posture -> `requirement` (policy built-in); `requirement` đi vào `buildConfinementRequest` -> Confinement Authority -> driver bwrap, cho cả pane herdr lẫn cli. Không còn `bwrapArgs` tự dựng trong `policies.mjs` (guard test). `resolvePostureInvocation` (`canApplyPosture` là dạng boolean của nó) là nơi duy nhất quyết: invocation khai `confinement.backend`, backend bật trong registry máy, executable chạy được; thiếu thì bind lọc candidate hoặc từ chối `posture-unavailable`, không chạy không confine. Nó cũng trả về invocation đã duyệt: khi `prefer` không nêu invocation, bind ghi đúng invocation cli thường đầu tiên mang được posture (không phải invocation cli đầu tiên của executor; `herdr-spawn` chỉ tính khi session ở trong herdr) vào binding, và `run.mjs` ghim đúng nó. Entry `prefer` nêu invocation thì giữ nguyên. Nên mọi invocation muốn được chọn phải khai `confinement`, và invocation của agent ghi state ngoài thư mục chỉ-đọc (codex, agy, pi) phải khai thêm `resourceBindings` private-home.
  5. **Tra capability.** `bind()` tìm `capabilities[domain:verb]` trước, rồi `capabilities[verb]`, nhưng entry chỉ thắng khi có `prefer` dùng được: slot chỉ có `description` (loại `fgos setup` ghi) không che bare-verb có `prefer`. Không có `prefer` ở đâu cả thì headless bị từ chối `headless-no-executor`; `fgos doctor` (`workflow-capabilities-configured`) cảnh báo đúng capability đó. Mặc định headless chỉ chạy được với Workflow đã khai `prefer`, không phải mọi Workflow `fgos setup` đã ghi slot.

  2. **Posture một đường.** `resolvePosture` chỉ ánh xạ posture -> `requirement` (policy built-in); `requirement` đi vào `buildConfinementRequest` -> Confinement Authority -> driver bwrap, cho cả pane herdr lẫn cli. Không còn `bwrapArgs` tự dựng trong `policies.mjs` (guard test). `resolvePostureInvocation` (`canApplyPosture` là dạng boolean của nó) là nơi duy nhất quyết: invocation khai `confinement.backend`, backend bật trong registry máy, executable chạy được; thiếu thì bind lọc candidate hoặc từ chối `posture-unavailable`, không chạy không confine. Nó cũng trả về invocation đã duyệt: khi `prefer` không nêu invocation, bind ghi đúng invocation cli thường đầu tiên mang được posture (không phải invocation cli đầu tiên của executor; `herdr-spawn` chỉ tính khi session ở trong herdr) vào binding, và `run.mjs` ghim đúng nó. Entry `prefer` nêu invocation thì giữ nguyên. Nên mọi invocation muốn được chọn phải khai `confinement`, và invocation của agent ghi state ngoài thư mục chỉ-đọc (codex, agy, pi) phải khai thêm `resourceBindings` private-home.
  5. **Tra capability.** `bind()` tìm `capabilities[domain:verb]` trước, rồi `capabilities[verb]`, nhưng entry chỉ thắng khi có `prefer` dùng được: slot chỉ có `description` (loại `fgos setup` ghi) không che bare-verb có `prefer`. Không có `prefer` ở đâu cả thì headless bị từ chối `headless-no-executor`; `fgos doctor` (`workflow-capabilities-configured`) cảnh báo đúng capability đó. Mặc định headless chỉ chạy được với Workflow đã khai `prefer`, không phải mọi Workflow `fgos setup` đã ghi slot.
  3. **Fallback quota.** `provider-limit` (herdr đọc màn hình qua detector của herdr, mặc định idle 5 phút nếu config không đặt `idleTimeoutMs`) -> `nextCandidate` đi tiếp `prefer[]` -> pane mới dưới assignment id `<unitRun>/<role>/<round>-fb<n>`; pane cũ giữ nguyên; `fallbackFrom` ghi lại; hết candidate thì outcome vẫn `provider-limit`. cli-spawn không có phát hiện limit nên headless không fallback (*cập nhật 2026-10-14:* nay có, qua câu hạn mức ở đuôi stderr, xem đoạn decision 0058 ở RUL65b). Pane idle (không `working`) quá 15 giây bị đọc màn hình để tìm credential chết (`AUTH_FAILURE_PATTERNS`, vd pi "OAuth refresh failed ... invalid_grant"): thấy thì cũng kết thúc `provider-limit` ngay, không chờ idle timeout, để walk sang candidate kế; classifier ghi quarantine `auth-token` kiểu `manual-clear` (tới khi người login lại và `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine`), không phải `quota-limit`. Quarantine quota dùng đúng thời gian reset provider ghi trên màn hình ("Resets in 24m1s", cả giờ/phút/giây), mặc định 1 giờ khi không ghi.
  4. **Pane confine cho cả năm họ** (claude, claude qua OpenRouter, codex, agy, pi): mỗi agent giữ state trong private home dựng từ account được lease; công thức và lý do ở [confinement-authority.md §13.1](./confinement-authority.md), account inventory toàn máy ở RUL65b (trên).
  - **Pane không nhận HOME riêng của worker.** Vòng herdr confine mở pane không kèm `HOME` private (launcher script tự `export` nó trước khi `exec`): shell của pane mà bắt đầu trong một home không có file khởi động thì zsh chạy trình hướng dẫn lần đầu và nuốt lệnh khởi chạy gõ ngay sau, nên vòng agy báo `foreground process ... does not match prepared command argv` dù argv không sai.
  - **Prompt delivery trong pane herdr (`inline` mặc định, `file-pointer` tuỳ chọn).** Mặc định `herdr-spawn` gửi toàn bộ nội dung `brief-<round>.md` trực tiếp vào pane qua `herdr agent prompt` (bracketed paste) để người quan sát thấy trọn vẹn prompt trong TUI, đồng thời vẫn ghi `brief-<round>.md` xuống đĩa kèm dòng trỏ đường dẫn phục hồi sau compaction; `promptDelivery: "file-pointer"` (hoặc `FGOS_HERDR_PROMPT_DELIVERY=file-pointer`) giữ cơ chế gõ con trỏ một dòng. `confirmBriefSubmitted` nhận diện cả paste chip thu gọn (`[Pasted text #1 +N lines]`, `[paste #1 +N lines]`, `[Paste]`, `#1 … +N lines`, menu `Pasted N lines`) ở vùng composer cuối màn hình; `SHELL_MANAGED_ENV` giữ nguyên `TERM`/`HERDR_PANE_ID` của pane mới (không để `TERM=dumb` hay `HERDR_PANE_ID` của process gọi ghi đè), `workerBaseEnv` loại bỏ `OMPCODE`/`OMP_PROFILE`/`PI_PROFILE`/`PI_CONFIG_FILES` của phiên cha, và `executors.xai` có thêm invocation `omp-herdr-vantt` chạy `omp` trong pane `bwrap`.
- **Bằng chứng:** [acceptance-herdr.md](../../plans/261002-1339-request-to-run-p6-herdr-posture-quota/reports/acceptance-herdr.md): ca 1 (Unit `reviewed`), 2 (reviewer bị chặn ghi repo, ghi được outbox), 3 (Workflow `architecture-advisory` 9 role trong pane, 4 họ provider), 4 (fallback, pane cũ giữ), 6 (headless cli cùng posture) Accepted; transport đọc từ `assignment.json`.
- **Giới hạn đã biết:**
  - Ca 5 (so cùng câu hỏi với engine cũ, tag `pre-engine-retirement`) **NOT RUN**: engine cũ cần Lead tự viết và authorize từng bước, nên "Lead-active" sẽ đo chính thao tác tay, không đo engine.
  - Ca 4 dùng màn hình limit **giả** (executor `fake-limit`); `DEFAULT_USAGE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` chưa đo trên màn hình limit thật của claude/codex. *Cập nhật 2026-10-05:* câu chữ đo được đầu tiên là của codex, "■ Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model." (đã thêm vào mẫu mặc định). Ngoài ra, thang liveness chỉ đọc màn hình khi tiến độ dừng, mà `working` tính là tiến độ, nên pane vẫn báo `working` nhưng đang kẹt ở lỗi nhà cung cấp chạy tới trần 15 phút không fallback (thấy khi dogfood mdview). Nay vòng thăm dò đọc 15 dòng cuối của agent đang `working` mỗi 30 giây và kết luận `provider-limit` khi cùng một dòng bắt đầu bằng dấu lỗi của CLI (`■`) và nêu điều kiện (`WORKING_STALL_PATTERNS`, chỉ câu chữ đã đo) còn nằm đó sau một khoảng thăm dò đầy đủ; chữ thường nhắc tới capacity hay rate limit không bị đụng tới.
  - **Trạng thái agent trong herdr (đo 2026-10-05, herdr 0.9.1-vantt.1).** herdr có đúng một nguồn trạng thái cho mỗi pane; fgos từng `pane report-agent --state working` lúc khởi động pane bị cô lập, nên fgos thành nguồn đó và `agent get` đứng yên ở `working` cả vòng (commit `2e9b53f6c` chỉ là đường vòng: đọc `agent explain` trước, hai lần gọi herdr mỗi nhịp thăm dò). Thí nghiệm trong pane thật: claude, codex, agy, pi chạy sau bwrap (không tách pid namespace) đều được herdr nhận ra không cần `HERDR_AGENT`, `agent get` khớp `agent explain`, và `agent prompt --wait` trả `done` sau ~2 giây; sau khi fgos báo `working`, `agent get` kẹt `working` còn `explain` nói `idle`, `agent prompt --wait` quá thời gian; `pane release-agent` trả lại quyền, trạng thái hồi phục sau vài giây. Nay fgos không báo trạng thái; chỉ khi herdr không nhận ra tiến trình là agent (sau 6 giây) mới báo, vì đó là cách duy nhất đánh địa chỉ nó (`ensureHerdrKnowsAgent`). Vòng thăm dò đọc `agent get`, chỉ hỏi `explain` khi `unknown`. Giới hạn: herdr chỉ biết `idle/working/blocked/done/unknown`, không biết lý do; manifest codex khớp ký tự xoay trong tiêu đề terminal là `working` (rule `osc_title_working`), nên pane codex kẹt ở lỗi nhà cung cấp vẫn là `working` và vẫn cần phần đọc màn hình ở trên. Mỗi vòng không bình thường để lại `herdr-diagnosis.json` (lời giải thích của chính herdr).
  - **Agent kẹt ở prompt chỉ người trả lời được (đo 2026-10-05, codex "Trust this folder?").** herdr báo đúng `blocked` (luật `trust_directory`), thang liveness kết luận `blocked` kèm dòng màn hình, nhưng bước settle coi mọi lỗi mang lớp `worker-timeout` là timeout nên run ghi `execution-timeout` và Unit ra `execution-failure`. Nay `blocked` (như `provider-limit`) đi thẳng qua `adapterOutcome`: `failure.code = blocked`, `outcome.category = blocked`, Unit outcome `blocked`, pane giữ nguyên, thông báo nêu cách sửa (trả lời prompt hoặc cấp trust cho project trong home của agent). Không thêm mẫu màn hình vì detector của herdr đã nhận ra màn hình này; màn hình không đọc được vẫn không phải bằng chứng.
  - Inventory account (`runner.providers.<provider>.accounts`) chỉ ở `~/.fgos/config.json` toàn máy; mỗi máy phải tự khai, `fgos setup` không tạo; `fgos doctor` (`confined-pane-accounts`) đọc inventory từ config toàn máy bất kể cwd (không cần project config) và chỉ ra pane thiếu entry; config toàn máy không đọc được thì check FAIL, nêu mã lỗi và đường dẫn.
  - bind chọn invocation herdr **đầu tiên** của executor; executor nhiều account cần luật chọn tường minh về sau.
Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.

| 1 | Cấu hình runner (file committed ở gốc repo) | Chính sách thực thi — LÀ CONFIG THỰC THI ĐƯỢC: ai sửa nó điều khiển tiến trình được spawn (đầu vào tin cậy) | `executor` — mẫu lệnh gọi trợ lý (thay thế `{prompt}`/`{model}` theo từng phần tử, không bao giờ qua shell), tùy chọn `adapter` (mặc định `cli-spawn`) · `executors` — catalog executor theo danh tính provider/cách gọi, không mang khẩu vị chất lượng · `modelPolicies` — bảng bắt buộc provider→tier→model với tier cung `nano|mini|standard|advanced|flagship|frontier` · `rigorToTier` — bảng bắt buộc ánh xạ đủ bốn mức cầu `low|standard|high|critical` sang tier cung · `capabilities.<name>.rigor` — sàn cầu tùy chọn, chỉ nâng; khối `capabilities.<name>.overrides` bị từ chối · `timeoutMs` — trần thời gian một worker · `confinement`/`confinementPolicies` — chính sách giam giữ · `capabilities` — catalog lời hứa hành vi và binding executor/invocation | yes | tự sinh khi vắng mặt tại đường dẫn mặc định (không kèm `--config`); `fgos setup` điền `rigorToTier`, `fgos doctor` kiểm bảng này và các khoá placement đã retired; một `--config <path>` tường minh trỏ vào đường vắng mặt vẫn báo lỗi ngay (`fgos discover`/`plan`; `fgos-runner` không còn `--config`, RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each)) |
| 1b | Provider-capacity inventory/state (slice 1) | Pool account cho một provider agent CLI khi provider đó có quota/capacity theo account. Inventory là machine-local secret-bearing config, không phải project policy; state/lease/quarantine là runtime-local evidence. | Inventory chỉ đọc từ `~/.fgos/config.json` tại `runner.providers.<provider>.accounts.<accountId>`; account là keyed object, không phải array. Slice 1 hỗ trợ `openai-codex` account với `label?` và `credentialSource: { kind: "codex-home", home }`; nay mỗi account khai đúng một trong `credentialSource` (một store cho mọi CLI, kind `codex-home` hoặc `home-files`) hoặc `credentialSources` (một store cho mỗi CLI, key là tên lệnh `codex`/`pi`/`omp`/`agy`; RUL80 (account trước, CLI sau: một login store cho mỗi CLI)). Account entry bị từ chối nếu khai placement/runtime policy (`executor`, `capability`, `model`, `modelTier`, `mutation`, `confinement`, `tool`, `fallback`, `runtimeClass`, `providerRuntimes`, ...). Project-local `.fgos/config.json` bị từ chối nếu chứa `runner.providers.*.accounts`. State ở `~/.fgos/runtime/provider-capacity/state.json`, lock ở `~/.fgos/runtime/provider-capacity/state.lock`. | no | vắng inventory nghĩa là mọi dispatch giữ hành vi cũ, không selection/lease |
| 2 | Nhánh đề xuất | Không gian kết quả của một worker, tên mang tiền tố nhận diện `fgw/<id>` | — | — | — |
| 3 | Bảng phục hồi | Lớp-lỗi → hành-động, máy đọc được | 8 lớp: hỏng-spawn, quá-giờ, chấm-trượt, hỏng-worktree, nhật-ký-hỏng, đề-xuất-bị-trả, việc-kẹt-do-crash, tranh-chấp-ghi → hành động ∈ thử-lại (có trần) / đỗ-lại / dừng; lớp LẠ → dừng (an toàn trước) | — | — |
| 4 | Bộ đếm chống-lặp (lifetime) | visitCount: số lần một việc vào `doing` TÍNH TỪ ĐẦU đời việc — dẫn xuất từ nhật ký sự kiện, không trường mới; dùng cho các bản ghi outcome/metric đã ship (KHÔNG dùng để chặn dispatch nữa — xem #4b) | — | — | — |
| 4b | Ngân sách cổng chống-lặp (kể từ can thiệp người) | visitsSinceLastHumanEvent: số lần việc vào `doing` **ở stage executing** TÍNH TỪ sự kiện người CUỐI CÙNG của chính việc đó — đây là con số CỔNG dùng để chặn/park dispatch (thay `visitCount` ở vai trò này); một can thiệp người (xem trigger-set) đưa ngân sách về lại đủ 3 cho vòng kế tiếp. Executing-phase-only scoping (claim-lock): trước đây, pick/take chỉ mở frontier (executing-phase), nên counting mọi `todo→doing` move tương đương dispatch attempts. Claim-lock cho phép `pick` cầm stage khác — claim-release cycle ở các stage đầu vòng (`discovery`/`exploring`/`planning`, cộng tên di sản `decompose`) không được tính vào ngân sách executing-phase (per claim-lock code-review finding) | — | — | trần mặc định 3, dùng chung `MAX_VISITS` |
| 5 | Cầu dao (breaker) | Số lần chấm-trượt liên tiếp trong MỘT lần chạy (bộ nhớ trong phiên, không dẫn xuất từ nhật ký — chủ đích, vì nhật ký không phân biệt người/máy ghi); trần mặc định 3, đếm RIÊNG cho từng việc dưới dispatch song song (một việc chấm-trượt không kéo cầu dao của việc khác). **Trơ trong `--once`:** một việc đỗ lại (park) tối đa sau `maxRetries` (mặc định 2) lần thử trong CÙNG một lượt `--once`, nên không bao giờ chạm trần 3 của cầu dao trong một lượt đơn — cầu dao chỉ có thể kéo khi có một cơ chế chia-sẻ/nhiều-lượt tích luỹ miss xuyên lượt (chưa xây, xem Open Gaps) | — | — | — |

| 7 | Quyền sở-hữu gốc | Ai đang cầm mọi việc CON của một gốc trong MỘT lượt chạy — gắn lúc con đầu tiên của gốc được nhận, xả khi gốc xong; sống trong bộ nhớ của lượt chạy, KHÔNG bền qua lượt chạy khác/tiến trình khác | một định danh (per lượt chạy) | — | chưa-chủ |
| 8 | Bản ghi output cục bộ (một file mỗi việc) | Lưu lại output của trợ lý cho MỌI lượt dispatch của một việc — đọc được sau khi console đã cuộn qua; không bao giờ vào cây committed. Cùng file còn nhận chunk stdout/stderr LIVE khi worker đang chạy (STR39, xem "Xem live output worker khi đang chạy") — `tail -f` thấy được ngay, không đợi khối kết-cục cuối | mỗi khối kết-cục: dấu thời gian, số lần thử, loại kết cục (đề xuất/quá-giờ/hỏng-spawn/…), output (khi trợ lý kịp sinh ra); xen giữa các khối kết-cục là chunk thô không bọc, ghi ngay khi đến | no (chỉ tồn tại sau lượt dispatch đầu tiên của việc) | — |

| 4 | Bộ đếm chống-lặp (lifetime) | visitCount: số lần một việc vào `doing` TÍNH TỪ ĐẦU đời việc — dẫn xuất từ nhật ký sự kiện, không trường mới; dùng cho các bản ghi outcome/metric đã ship (KHÔNG dùng để chặn dispatch nữa — xem #4b) | — | — | — |

| 8 | Bản ghi output cục bộ (một file mỗi việc) | Lưu lại output của trợ lý cho MỌI lượt dispatch của một việc — đọc được sau khi console đã cuộn qua; không bao giờ vào cây committed. | 9 | Candidate (Gate A, self-improve loop STR13 Slice 1) | Một việc mang ít nhất một bản ghi friction chưa ngã-ngũ, xếp hạng làm ứng viên tự cải thiện — dẫn xuất TỪ friction đã ghi, không phải một bản ghi độc lập, không bền qua lần `evolve` khác | id, disposition, errorClass, layer, detail, attempts (tất cả lấy từ bản ghi friction MỚI NHẤT theo dấu thời gian của id đó khi id có nhiều bản ghi chưa ngã-ngũ), score (cộng dồn TOÀN BỘ bản ghi chưa ngã-ngũ của id đó, không chỉ bản mới nhất) | — | dẫn xuất mỗi lần gọi `evolve` |
| 10 | Phán quyết Iron Law (self-improve loop STR13 Slice 2/3) | Kết quả của phép tính hai-cửa (module + từ khóa) trên MỘT candidate fix — dẫn xuất thuần từ đầu vào truyền vào, không bền. unit.sample: - **RUL73 (dispatch KHÔNG biết Work, domain hay bước — tầng Work tra rồi truyền vào; Work không còn `stage`).** `src/runner/dispatch/**` và `src/runner/execution/**` không import `
unit.text:
- **RUL73 (dispatch KHÔNG biết Work, domain hay bước — tầng Work tra rồi truyền vào; Work không còn `stage`).** `src/runner/dispatch/**` và `src/runner/execution/**` không import `src/state/**`, `src/workflow/**` hay bất kỳ module tầng Work (`work-compat`, `work-dispatch`, `operation-choice`, `loop`, `claim-port`, `prompt-templates`, `intake/`, `verbs/`), và không chứa literal tên domain/bước (guard `test/architecture.test.mjs`, tên đọc từ `domains/*/` trên đĩa). Cụ thể:
  1. Operation/taskSpec/skill của một bước đến từ định nghĩa Workflow (`domains/<d>/workflows/*.yaml`, `steps[].operations`/`skill`), tầng Work đọc qua `src/state/domain-registry.mjs` rồi đưa vào `buildAssignment({ domain, stage, operation, operations })`. Dispatch kiểm `operation ∈ operations` (lỗi `unknown operation ... for stage ...`), ghi danh sách hợp lệ vào `provenance.declared.legalOperations`; `executeAssignment` từ chối một Assignment declared không mang danh sách đó hoặc có `operation` ngoài danh sách (và `dispatch: human-only`). unit.sample: - **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the
unit.text:
- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One lock per provider account under `/account-locks///`, separate from the state lock, in the same append-only generation format. A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The holder records the pid of the renewal child it started: a dead holder with a live child keeps the lock, so a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. Left open: the login store per CLI (RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI)) is checked only by the lease at dispatch, after the unit run exists; `capacityProviderOf` derives the provider from the executor entry and can differ from the lease's for an executor that declares no `providerModel` (every configured executor declares one); `fgos workflow start` has no `--account`. - **RUL92 (a writing seat is not run again over its own partial writes after a provider limit, 2026-10-14).** At every launch of a seat that writes (a resumed launch included), the runner records the worktree's HEAD and the content of every path `git status` sees as changed (`writeBaseline` on the attempt, `src/runner/execution/partial-writes.mjs`; `.fgos/` left out, a symlink by its target, an unreadable file by size and mtime). When the seat stops on a provider limit and the worktree differs (a write, rename, delete, a further change to a file already dirty, a moved HEAD), it is not rotated to another account nor walked to another candidate: the seat ends `provider-limit` with `fallbackExhausted: { reason: partial-writes, paths, headMoved }` and `retryStopped` on the attempt, for a person to keep, finish or undo the changes and resume. This check runs before the pinned stop of RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run), so a pinned seat still names what it changed (`accountPinned`). A read-only seat records no baseline and rotates as before (its sandbox keeps the worktree; a concurrent `verify` write never stops it), as does a writing seat that left the worktree as it was; a baseline git could not take stops the retry. Not seen: gitignored paths, `.fgos/` inside the worktree, changes inside a nested repository or a dirty submodule, a mode-only change to a file already dirty; none of them reaches the runner's commit, which takes only the write scope. - **RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each, 2026-10-14; ends the `spawnWorker` purpose door of RUL68 (2 tầng dispatch) and the `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` entries of RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed) for `loop.mjs`, `work-dispatch.mjs` and `fanout-batch.mjs`).** `spawnWorker` (`src/runner/work-dispatch.mjs`) builds the item's Unit with `workUnitFor` and runs it through `runUnit` in the item's worktree, with `session { headless: true, herdrPresent: false }` (the loop never opens a pane, even when the runner itself runs inside herdr); `fanout-batch.mjs` does the same per candidate after `pick`, then `fgos return` on `pass` (no `--worker-verified-sha`: return judges the Unit run's commit) or `return --to blocked` otherwise, reporting each `fired` entry as `{id, unitRunId, outcome, commit}`. The worker runs confined and never commits; the Unit run commits a passing round inside its `writes` (`['**']` for a step), and the loop reads `commit` (`runner`, `none`, or `self` when HEAD moved without a runner commit) instead of committing itself. A step Unit names its capability as its domain's Workflow units do, `:` (`coding:discover`), except the coding executing step, which keeps `code:implement`; `bind()` falls back to the bare verb, and `fgos doctor`'s `workflow-capabilities-configured` also names `code:implement` (`RUNNER_LOOP_CAPABILITY_USES`). The worker config is the repo's `.fgos/config.json` (snapshotted into `unit.json`): `fgos-runner` has no `--config` any more. Outcomes map onto the recovery matrix (`src/runner/recovery.mjs`): a failed runner commit, or an index staged before launch, is `worktree-fail`; a timeout `worker-timeout`; a command that cannot start `worker-spawn-fail`; every candidate at its provider limit `provider-limit` (park); a refusal before any worker started `no-executor` (park, the message names `runner.capabilities[""].prefer`), so one capability without a runnable pool never halts the runner; a round that ran, did not pass and left uncommitted files `worker-failed` (retry), so goal-check never judges files that are not on the branch; a round that did not pass and left nothing resolves with `commit: none` and goal-check decides on the branch as it stands. A round that stopped over its own partial writes (RUL92 (a writing seat is not run again over its own partial writes after a provider limit)) or whose runner commit failed keeps its worktree: the loop notes `{unitRunId, worktree}` under `.fgos/runtime/runner-resume/.json`, and the item's next attempt (a retry, or a later dispatch once the item is back at `todo`) resumes that same Unit run there, so a failed commit is committed again without spawning the agent; the note is checked against `unit.json` (same Unit id, worktree still checked out on `fgw/`) and dropped once the run no longer needs it. The Unit's rigor comes from the operation, then the item's `rigor`, with `risk: heavy` read as `high` only when no `rigor` is declared; bind's floor raises `low` to `standard`. The item's `refs` and `docsRef` enter the Unit only as safe repo-relative paths (others are dropped with a warning that reaches the loop log), and its `prefer` names the step's executor only when that executor is registered. The executor dispatch event carries `unitRunId`; the item log names the run the moment it exists and where its output is captured (`protected/capture/` while it runs, `stdout.log` once it settles), since a Unit run streams nothing back; a write into the main checkout during the round reaches the loop log as a `stray-write-correlated` warning. A pane run's `stdout.log` holds the settled report's text, so a worker run in a pane must put its `fgos-verdict`/`fgos-discovered` fences in its report; the loop reads the first non-empty of report, `stdout.log` and claim summary, never several. The startup reap keeps a 0-commit `fgw/` branch that a killed round still has checked out, with its uncommitted work, instead of failing on the branch delete. Not done: the loop does not resume a Unit run left `running` by a killed runner (the run id is in the item log; `fgos run --resume `); a worker detached from a killed runner may outlive it; a commit subject falls back to `producer changes` when the worker wrote no claim. - **RUL94 (a Work driver step runs as a Unit: the step's declared operation, pinned inputs, and a verdict bound to their bytes, 2026-10-14; ends the `operation-choice.mjs` entry of `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` from RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed)).** A driver step of a work item (`fgos plan --validate`, the runner loop's validate-plan and secondary operations) is built by `workUnitFor` and run through `runUnit`, never by `executeAssignment` (`src/runner/operation-choice.mjs`). `runUnit` takes `declared: {workId, domain, workflow, stage, operation, operations}` (the step's operation objects), `pinInputs` (absolute paths) and `runnerConfig` (the config the caller resolved, snapshotted instead of `.fgos/config.json`, so one step reads one config); `declared` and `pinInputs` are kept in `unit.json` and a resume reads them, and the pattern, from there. Refused before the unit directory exists: an operation the step does not declare, a `human-only` one, a stamped mutation that disagrees with the unit's `writes` (read-only exactly when it writes nothing), and any pattern that does not resolve to `solo`. Only the producer seat carries the operation: its assignment has the operation's role and normalizer stamp (`mutation`, `evidence`, `resultKind`, `onAdvance`, built by `declaredOperationFields` in `src/runner/dispatch/assignment.mjs`, shared with `buildAssignment`), the seat name stays in `provenance.role`, and `policy.rigor` is the unit's rigor. At launch the dispatch hashes each pin into `inputDigests[{path, root, rel, sha256}]` in `run.json` and `result.json`; a pin is read only when its real path lies in the main checkout or a worktree git lists (not one that became a symlink), against the innermost such root, else its `sha256` is `null` and nothing is read. The verdict walker (`findLatestAssignmentRunResult`) reads flat and nested layouts through `listAssignmentRuns`, filters by `operation`, takes only a unit run's producer seat, and compares the current `plan.md` by `rel` and digest; a pinned digest decides alone (no mtime pre-filter), so a plan merged byte for byte into another checkout still matches, and `planContentHash` is only read on results from before this rule. The driver hands the producer's own RunResult and seat assignment to `interpretAssignmentRunResult`, stops on a unit with no result or whose runner commit failed (`unit-commit-failed`), and never turns an item ref naming another run's output (`unit-run:`, `gate-answer:`) into an input. The worker is confined (`session: {headless: true, herdrPresent: false}`): a read-only operation cannot write the checkout, and a machine with no confinement backend stops the step (`unit-refused-posture-unavailable`). A unit with `rigor: low` is raised to `standard` by bind's floor. Not done here: a pin resolved through `process.cwd()` first (`resolveContentRoot`) can differ from the plan in the item worktree a secondary operation runs in. - **RUL95 (dispatch takes generic inputs only; Work is a consumer, 2026-10-14; decision 0063, replaces the input part of RUL73 (dispatch does not know Work).2 and closes the `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` list of RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed)).** `src/runner/dispatch/**`, `src/runner/execution/**`, `src/runner/dispatch.mjs` and `src/workflow/**` never handle a Work item. Rigor and domain are the assignment's own fields: `resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy` reads `assignment.rigor` where it read `work.rigor`/`work.risk` (first explicit source may pick it, after an operation rigor it only raises, the capability floor and tier rules are unchanged; provenance scope `assignment`) and `assignment.domain` for the `:review` capability floor, so a declared Unit step (whose seat carries `domain`) gets that floor again. The Work layer folds an item's `rigor` and `risk: heavy` into one rigor (`workRigorFor`). `decide --work` gets a hint from the Work layer, `workDispatchHint`/`resolveWorkForDispatch` → `{workExecutorId, agentType, rigor?, domain?}`, passed to `compileDispatchPlan({workId, workHint})`; fan-out uses the same hint. `workDispatchContext` returns only `{capabilityHints, agentType}`. `buildAssignment`, `resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`, `compileDispatchPlan`, `decideExecutorCli`, `executeExecutorCli` and `executeAssignment` refuse a `work`, `workItem` or `workExecutorId` input (`RunnerConfigError` "takes no Work item") instead of ignoring it; `decideExecutorCli` and `compileDispatchPlan` name the `--work` selector `workId`. `executeExecutorCli` no longer runs an unregistered executor id because a Work item rode along (`executor-not-found`). A domain's contract harness (ADR-007) is loaded only by the Work layer (`domainHarnessFor(work, {domain})`, only for a registered domain at a declared step; `loadHarnessModule` treats a module that fails to import as no harness), and a caller hands it to the inline `buildAssignment` as `options.domainHarness`; dispatch still re-validates the enriched contract and records `domain-harness-seam`. No production path builds an inline assignment for a Work item today (none did before either: the only inline caller is `probe-account`), so the seam runs only in tests. The guard (`test/architecture.test.mjs`) refuses, outside comments and other string text, any identifier or property named `work`, `workItem` or `docsRef` (identifier escapes such as `\u0077ork` are decoded first), any string that is exactly one of those names (a computed or quoted key, `Reflect.get(o, 'work')`, a key comparison; only the pinned uses are allowed: the `--work` selector's type in `plan.mjs` and the refused option names in `assignment-policy.mjs`), and any `resolveContentRoot(` call in the guarded files; `src/state/**` counts as Work layer for the transitive import guard, except one pinned edge (`worktree.mjs` takes only `StoreError` from `src/state/store.mjs`); imports are read with optional whitespace, comments blanked, `?query` dropped, and absolute paths and `file:` URLs resolved; the guarded folders may hold only plain `.mjs` files (no `.js`/`.cjs`/TypeScript source, no symlink); the shared source lexer treats a slash after a block's closing brace as a regular expression, so its quotes cannot hide the code after it; it also refuses an `import()`/`require()` whose specifier is not one plain literal, `createRequire`, `eval`, `Function(...)` (with or without `new`) and an import of `module`, `vm` or `worker_threads` (with or without `node:`), except the loads pinned one by one in a named allowlist entry with its reason (`provider-credential-renewal.mjs`: `createRequire` for `node:sqlite`); one more load in an allowlisted file fails too. The call-site guard also counts a string that is exactly a door's name (`d['executeAssignment'](a)`) and an escaped name as a use, and compares each run door with exactly its named callers (`executeAssignment`: `execution/run.mjs`, `dispatch/cli.mjs`; `executeExecutorCli`: `dispatch/assignment-runner.mjs`; `commitUnitWork`: `execution/run.mjs`; `executeThroughConfinement`: `dispatch/cli.mjs`), both ways. Not covered: a name built at run time (`opts[k]`, `opts['wo' + 'rk']`, `globalThis['ev' + 'al']`), nested inputs (`options.work`, `assignment.work`; nothing reads them), and code outside the guarded files that reaches into dispatch's internals. - **RUL96 (one run may take its own timeout, from 1m to 4h; its private home and worktree lock last as long, 2026-10-15).** A unit run's seats are dispatched with `runner.timeoutMs` unless the run asks for its own: `fgos run --timeout ` (a whole number and one unit, `ms|s|m|h`: `90m`, `5400s`), a `timeoutMs` key on an `--override` object (`--timeout` adds it to every override that names none, and an unscoped one when none is unscoped, as `--effort` does), or a Unit's `timeoutMs` (whole milliseconds; a units file and a Workflow unit template carry it too, a template's value is checked when the definition loads). `bind()` resolves override, then unit, into `binding.timeoutMs` with `provenance.timeoutMs { value, source: override: | unit | none }`; a value outside the range is a refused binding (`run-timeout`), and an override's value is checked before the unit run exists. The value lives in `unit.json` (`overrides`, `unit`, and every recorded binding), so a resume dispatches with it and `--timeout` is refused with `--resume`; `runUnit` hands it to `executeAssignment` (`opts.timeoutMs ?? cfg.timeoutMs`), which already threads it to the worker kill, the pane poll and the dispatch lock. Range (`src/runner/dispatch/run-timeout.mjs`): the 1m floor keeps a typo (`90s` for `90m`) from killing a turn at once; the 4h ceiling, four times the heaviest turn seen, bounds how long a hung worker holds its worktree's lock and a copy of an account login, and `runner.timeoutMs` above it is refused when the config loads, so the default obeys it too. The confinement reaper keeps a home whose dispatcher pid is alive and has no pane until `createdAt + max(maxAgeMs, min(marker.timeoutMs, 4h) + 10m)` (the bwrap driver records the dispatch's `timeoutMs` in the ownership marker; a marker without one keeps the 1h rule; a dead dispatcher's home goes at once, a pane-retained home is unchanged), so a pane-less run longer than an hour is no longer reaped mid-turn. The per-worktree dispatch lock (`.fgos/dispatch--.lock`, composite `pid:acquiredAtMs:rand` holder) records the `ttlMs` its holder took and keeps it across renewals; a contender judges a live composite holder by the longer of its own ttl and the holder's, so a dispatch with a shorter timeout never takes the lock of a longer run that renews only every third of its own timeout; the recorded ttl is honoured only up to the 4h ceiling. Other lock identities are judged as before. Residual: a holder killed without releasing whose pid was reused reads as live (no process start time is recorded), so it now blocks the worktree for up to its own ttl (at most 4h) instead of the contender's; `fgos dispatch reconcile` clears such a lock by hand. `--override` passed with `--resume` is ignored, as for every override key (the run keeps `unit.json#overrides`). - **RUL97 (a Unit may sync a base ref first: the runner merges it, the worker only edits the conflicted files, 2026-10-15).** A Unit may carry `syncBase` (a branch, tag or commit name: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `/`, `-`, not starting with `-` or `/`, no `..`); it needs `writes` and a linked worktree, and `fgos run --sync ` sets it (with a prompt: sync, then the task; without one: a sync-only Unit, `syncOnly: true`, whose objective is `Merge into this branch.`). The ref is resolved to a commit once, before the unit run exists (a ref naming no commit, or a run from the main checkout, leaves nothing behind), and `unit.json#sync` keeps `{ ref, sha, status, head?, conflicts?, mergeStaged?, commit? }`; a resume merges that sha, never the ref again. Before any seat runs, the runner merges it with the trusted git of RUL85 (the runner commits only the Unit's write scope) — `merge --no-commit --no-ff`, rerere and autostash off — in `src/runner/execution/commit-unit-work.mjs` (`startSyncMerge`, `finishSyncMerge`, `syncMergeState`), orchestrated by `src/runner/execution/unit-sync.mjs`: already in the branch is `up-to-date`; a clean merge is committed by the runner as `chore(sync): merge ` (status `merged`; a commit that is not the merge of `sha` over `head` holding exactly what the merge staged — a hook added a file — fails `committed-set-mismatch` as `execution-failure`, stays on the branch, and the resume is refused until a person takes it off) and the Unit goes on to its pattern, or passes at once when sync-only; a sync never brings the base side of `.fgos/` in: every `.fgos/**` path the merge staged or left conflicted, clean or not, is put back to the branch side (HEAD), a path the base deleted is kept and a path only the base has is not taken — ADR0020 (a worker branch never commits `.fgos/`), the side `fgos-write-rejected` at approve resolves to the target for a `.fgos/` path the branch left unchanged, on every branch, not only `fgw/*`; any other conflict leaves the merge open (status `conflicted`), puts the conflicted paths the scope does not already cover in scope only while the merge is open (`sync.scopeAdded`, read by the effective scope only while `sync.status === 'conflicted'`; `writeScope` itself stays as declared, so a later round cannot write them), and appends a `## Merge to finish` section to the writing seat's brief naming them and telling it never to run git. A refused start leaves no merge open and ends the run: `merge-in-progress` (a merge someone else opened), `foreign-staged-index`, `merge-refused` (git would not start, e.g. a dirty file it would overwrite), `hook-refused` (the pre-commit hook of the main checkout's hooks path refused the clean merge commit; told apart from a git failure by running that hook once more as git runs it, and its words are the detail), `unscopable-conflict-path` (a conflicted path the scope normalizer of RUL84 (one write-scope matcher) would read differently — `*`, a leading `:`, `\`, surrounding whitespace — or holding a control character, since it is also printed into the brief; the merge is aborted) as `policy-refusal`, and `git-error` as `execution-failure`. While the merge is open, the preflight of a writing seat counts only the open MERGE_HEAD equal to `sync.sha` over `sync.head` as the run's own: its conflicted and merge-staged paths are neither a foreign index nor `preExistingInScope`; any other open merge refuses a writing seat (`merge-in-progress`) and `commitUnitWork` never commits over one. After a passing round the runner concludes the merge before the round's own commit: a conflicted file that still holds a line opening with seven or more `<`, `|` or `>` (a larger `conflict-marker-size` included; a file holding a NUL byte is read as binary and not checked) fails the commit `conflict-markers` with `paths`, stages nothing and keeps the merge, so `fgos run --resume` only commits once a person removed them (RUL86 (`fgos run --resume` after a failed runner commit only commits)); otherwise it stages the conflicted paths, refuses an index holding anything the merge did not stage (`staged-set-mismatch`, taking back what it staged itself, e.g. a conflicted file the worker turned into a directory), commits with MERGE_HEAD as second parent (a refusing pre-commit hook fails it `hook-refused` with the hook's words and keeps the merge; each `fgos run --resume` tries the commit once, never in a loop), checks parents and committed set (`committed-set-mismatch`), and then commits the rest of the round inside the scope as usual. The round's `commit` carries the merge's own record under `sync`; `runUnit` returns `sync` beside `outcome`; a sync-only unit that needed no worker returns one result `{ role: 'sync', round: 0, commit }` (no `verify`, as for `solo`). A round that did not pass keeps the merge open; a resume checks it first: still open, it runs the seat again over it; concluded by hand (its sha in the branch), it is `merged`; aborted, or HEAD moved, the resume is refused and names the merge. A run that died between starting git and recording the result adopts its own open merge on resume; a first start never adopts one. A resumed sync-only run that was `up-to-date` or `merged` passes again without a worker. Settlement: the writing seat over an open merge carries `assignment.syncConflicts`; those files, dirty at launch, changed during the turn and inside its scope, count as its evidence (`evidence.editedSyncConflicts`), so a seat that only resolves conflicts is not scored `verdict-inconclusive`. Any other file dirty at launch that a seat rewrites still is no evidence, with or without a sync. A units file (`fgos workflow start --units`) naming `syncBase` is refused: a workflow unit's worktree starts from its dependency's branch, and a sync there is not built. Not done: an inline producer over an open merge (inline rounds have no runner commit), a modify/delete conflict whose worker deletes the file is concluded as a deletion.

successor.text:
- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One lock per provider account under `/account-locks///`, separate from the state lock, in the same append-only generation format. A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The holder records the pid of the renewal child it started: a dead holder with a live child keeps the lock, so a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). Lệnh `fgos workflow start` ở chế độ detached vẫn trả về mã 0 khi tiến trình daemon được khởi chạy thành công. Định dạng envelope JSON stdout `fgos.v1` giữ nguyên vẹn 100%. - **RUL100 (Doctor check `executor-posture-coverage` chẩn đoán posture readiness của các executor, 2026-10-15).** Check doctor `executor-posture-coverage` kiểm tra tĩnh khả năng áp dụng posture cho các core capabilities (`execute`, `code:implement`) và mọi capability khai báo pool agent (`prefer`). Quá trình kiểm tra chạy hoàn toàn khô qua `bind()`, không spawn tiến trình, không tạo pane herdr, không kích hoạt sandbox. Khi một capability có executor thiếu sandbox bwrap, check báo lỗi `posture-unavailable` (`passed: false`). Khi một capability thiếu pool (`headless-no-executor` / `no-candidate`), check chỉ phát cảnh báo (`passed: true`, tiền tố `warning:`) hướng dẫn khai báo `runner.capabilities..prefer`.
