Not seen: gitignored paths, `.fgos/` inside the worktree, changes inside a nested repository or a dirty submodule, a mode-only change to a file already dirty; none of them reaches the runner's commit, which takes only the write scope. - **RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each, 2026-10-14; ends the `spawnWorker` purpose door of RUL68 (2 tầng dispatch) and the `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` entries of RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed) for `loop.mjs`, `work-dispatch.mjs` and `fanout-batch.mjs`).** `spawnWorker` (`src/runner/work-dispatch.mjs`) builds the item's Unit with `workUnitFor` and runs it through `runUnit` in the item's worktree, with `session { headless: true, herdrPresent: false }` (the loop never opens a pane, even when the runner itself runs inside herdr); `fanout-batch.mjs` does the same per candidate after `pick`, then `fgos return` on `pass` (no `--worker-verified-sha`: return judges the Unit run's commit) or `return --to blocked` otherwise, reporting each `fired` entry as `{id, unitRunId, outcome, commit}`. The worker runs confined and never commits; the Unit run commits a passing round inside its `writes` (`['**']` for a step), and the loop reads `commit` (`runner`, `none`, or `self` when HEAD moved without a runner commit) instead of committing itself. A step Unit names its capability as its domain's Workflow units do, `:` (`coding:discover`), except the coding executing step, which keeps `code:implement`; `bind()` falls back to the bare verb, and `fgos doctor`'s `workflow-capabilities-configured` also names `code:implement` (`RUNNER_LOOP_CAPABILITY_USES`). The worker config is the repo's `.fgos/config.json` (snapshotted into `unit.json`): `fgos-runner` has no `--config` any more. Outcomes map onto the recovery matrix (`src/runner/recovery.mjs`): a failed runner commit, or an index staged before launch, is `worktree-fail`; a timeout `worker-timeout`; a command that cannot start `worker-spawn-fail`; every candidate at its provider limit `provider-limit` (park); a refusal before any worker started `no-executor` (park, the message names `runner.capabilities[""].prefer`), so one capability without a runnable pool never halts the runner; a round that ran, did not pass and left uncommitted files `worker-failed` (retry), so goal-check never judges files that are not on the branch; a round that did not pass and left nothing resolves with `commit: none` and goal-check decides on the branch as it stands. A round that stopped over its own partial writes (RUL92 (a writing seat is not run again over its own partial writes after a provider limit)) or whose runner commit failed keeps its worktree: the loop notes `{unitRunId, worktree}` under `.fgos/runtime/runner-resume/.json`, and the item's next attempt (a retry, or a later dispatch once the item is back at `todo`) resumes that same Unit run there, so a failed commit is committed again without spawning the agent; the note is checked against `unit.json` (same Unit id, worktree still checked out on `fgw/`) and dropped once the run no longer needs it. The Unit's rigor comes from the operation, then the item's `rigor`, with `risk: heavy` read as `high` only when no `rigor` is declared; bind's floor raises `low` to `standard`. The item's `refs` and `docsRef` enter the Unit only as safe repo-relative paths (others are dropped with a warning that reaches the loop log), and its `prefer` names the step's executor only when that executor is registered. The executor dispatch event carries `unitRunId`; the item log names the run the moment it exists and where its output is captured (`protected/capture/` while it runs, `stdout.log` once it settles), since a Unit run streams nothing back; a write into the main checkout during the round reaches the loop log as a `stray-write-correlated` warning. A pane run's `stdout.log` holds the settled report's text, so a worker run in a pane must put its `fgos-verdict`/`fgos-discovered` fences in its report; the loop reads the first non-empty of report, `stdout.log` and claim summary, never several. The startup reap keeps a 0-commit `fgw/` branch that a killed round still has checked out, with its uncommitted work, instead of failing on the branch delete. Not done: the loop does not resume a Unit run left `running` by a killed runner (the run id is in the item log; `fgos run --resume `); a worker detached from a killed runner may outlive it; a commit subject falls back to `producer changes` when the worker wrote no claim. - **RUL94 (a Work driver step runs as a Unit: the step's declared operation, pinned inputs, and a verdict bound to their bytes, 2026-10-14; ends the `operation-choice.mjs` entry of `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` from RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed)).** A driver step of a work item (`fgos plan --validate`, the runner loop's validate-plan and secondary operations) is built by `workUnitFor` and run through `runUnit`, never by `executeAssignment` (`src/runner/operation-choice.mjs`). `runUnit` takes `declared: {workId, domain, workflow, stage, operation, operations}` (the step's operation objects), `pinInputs` (absolute paths) and `runnerConfig` (the config the caller resolved, snapshotted instead of `.fgos/config.json`, so one step reads one config); `declared` and `pinInputs` are kept in `unit.json` and a resume reads them, and the pattern, from there. Refused before the unit directory exists: an operation the step does not declare, a `human-only` one, a stamped mutation that disagrees with the unit's `writes` (read-only exactly when it writes nothing), and any pattern that does not resolve to `solo`. Only the producer seat carries the operation: its assignment has the operation's role and normalizer stamp (`mutation`, `evidence`, `resultKind`, `onAdvance`, built by `declaredOperationFields` in `src/runner/dispatch/assignment.mjs`, shared with `buildAssignment`), the seat name stays in `provenance.role`, and `policy.rigor` is the unit's rigor. At launch the dispatch hashes each pin into `inputDigests[{path, root, rel, sha256}]` in `run.json` and `result.json`; a pin is read only when its real path lies in the main checkout or a worktree git lists (not one that became a symlink), against the innermost such root, else its `sha256` is `null` and nothing is read. The verdict walker (`findLatestAssignmentRunResult`) reads flat and nested layouts through `listAssignmentRuns`, filters by `operation`, takes only a unit run's producer seat, and compares the current `plan.md` by `rel` and digest; a pinned digest decides alone (no mtime pre-filter), so a plan merged byte for byte into another checkout still matches, and `planContentHash` is only read on results from before this rule. The driver hands the producer's own RunResult and seat assignment to `interpretAssignmentRunResult`, stops on a unit with no result or whose runner commit failed (`unit-commit-failed`), and never turns an item ref naming another run's output (`unit-run:`, `gate-answer:`) into an input. The worker is confined (`session: {headless: true, herdrPresent: false}`): a read-only operation cannot write the checkout, and a machine with no confinement backend stops the step (`unit-refused-posture-unavailable`). A unit with `rigor: low` is raised to `standard` by bind's floor. Not done here: a pin resolved through `process.cwd()` first (`resolveContentRoot`) can differ from the plan in the item worktree a secondary operation runs in. - **RUL95 (dispatch takes generic inputs only; Work is a consumer, 2026-10-14; decision 0063, replaces the input part of RUL73 (dispatch does not know Work).2 and closes the `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` list of RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed)).** `src/runner/dispatch/**`, `src/runner/execution/**`, `src/runner/dispatch.mjs` and `src/workflow/**` never handle a Work item. Rigor and domain are the assignment's own fields: `resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy` reads `assignment.rigor` where it read `work.rigor`/`work.risk` (first explicit source may pick it, after an operation rigor it only raises, the capability floor and tier rules are unchanged; provenance scope `assignment`) and `assignment.domain` for the `:review` capability floor, so a declared Unit step (whose seat carries `domain`) gets that floor again. The Work layer folds an item's `rigor` and `risk: heavy` into one rigor (`workRigorFor`). `decide --work` gets a hint from the Work layer, `workDispatchHint`/`resolveWorkForDispatch` → `{workExecutorId, agentType, rigor?, domain?}`, passed to `compileDispatchPlan({workId, workHint})`; fan-out uses the same hint. `workDispatchContext` returns only `{capabilityHints, agentType}`. `buildAssignment`, `resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`, `compileDispatchPlan`, `decideExecutorCli`, `executeExecutorCli` and `executeAssignment` refuse a `work`, `workItem` or `workExecutorId` input (`RunnerConfigError` "takes no Work item") instead of ignoring it; `decideExecutorCli` and `compileDispatchPlan` name the `--work` selector `workId`. `executeExecutorCli` no longer runs an unregistered executor id because a Work item rode along (`executor-not-found`). A domain's contract harness (ADR-007) is loaded only by the Work layer (`domainHarnessFor(work, {domain})`, only for a registered domain at a declared step; `loadHarnessModule` treats a module that fails to import as no harness), and a caller hands it to the inline `buildAssignment` as `options.domainHarness`; dispatch still re-validates the enriched contract and records `domain-harness-seam`. No production path builds an inline assignment for a Work item today (none did before either: the only inline caller is `probe-account`), so the seam runs only in tests. The guard (`test/architecture.test.mjs`) refuses, outside comments and other string text, any identifier or property named `work`, `workItem` or `docsRef` (identifier escapes such as `\u0077ork` are decoded first), any string that is exactly one of those names (a computed or quoted key, `Reflect.get(o, 'work')`, a key comparison; only the pinned uses are allowed: the `--work` selector's type in `plan.mjs` and the refused option names in `assignment-policy.mjs`), and any `resolveContentRoot(` call in the guarded files; `src/state/**` counts as Work layer for the transitive import guard, except one pinned edge (`worktree.mjs` takes only `StoreError` from `src/state/store.mjs`); imports are read with optional whitespace, comments blanked, `?query` dropped, and absolute paths and `file:` URLs resolved; the guarded folders may hold only plain `.mjs` files (no `.js`/`.cjs`/TypeScript source, no symlink); the shared source lexer treats a slash after a block's closing brace as a regular expression, so its quotes cannot hide the code after it; it also refuses an `import()`/`require()` whose specifier is not one plain literal, `createRequire`, `eval`, `Function(...)` (with or without `new`) and an import of `module`, `vm` or `worker_threads` (with or without `node:`), except the loads pinned one by one in a named allowlist entry with its reason (`provider-credential-renewal.mjs`: `createRequire` for `node:sqlite`); one more load in an allowlisted file fails too. The call-site guard also counts a string that is exactly a door's name (`d['executeAssignment'](a)`) and an escaped name as a use, and compares each run door with exactly its named callers (`executeAssignment`: `execution/run.mjs`, `dispatch/cli.mjs`; `executeExecutorCli`: `dispatch/assignment-runner.mjs`; `commitUnitWork`: `execution/run.mjs`; `executeThroughConfinement`: `dispatch/cli.mjs`), both ways. Not covered: a name built at run time (`opts[k]`, `opts['wo' + 'rk']`, `globalThis['ev' + 'al']`), nested inputs (`options.work`, `assignment.work`; nothing reads them), and code outside the guarded files that reaches into dispatch's internals. - **RUL96 (one run may take its own timeout, from 1m to 4h; its private home and worktree lock last as long, 2026-10-15).** A unit run's seats are dispatched with `runner.timeoutMs` unless the run asks for its own: `fgos run --timeout ` (a whole number and one unit, `ms|s|m|h`: `90m`, `5400s`), a `timeoutMs` key on an `--override` object (`--timeout` adds it to every override that names none, and an unscoped one when none is unscoped, as `--effort` does), or a Unit's `timeoutMs` (whole milliseconds; a units file and a Workflow unit template carry it too, a template's value is checked when the definition loads). `bind()` resolves override, then unit, into `binding.timeoutMs` with `provenance.timeoutMs { value, source: override: | unit | none }`; a value outside the range is a refused binding (`run-timeout`), and an override's value is checked before the unit run exists. The value lives in `unit.json` (`overrides`, `unit`, and every recorded binding), so a resume dispatches with it and `--timeout` is refused with `--resume`; `runUnit` hands it to `executeAssignment` (`opts.timeoutMs ?? cfg.timeoutMs`), which already threads it to the worker kill, the pane poll and the dispatch lock. Range (`src/runner/dispatch/run-timeout.mjs`): the 1m floor keeps a typo (`90s` for `90m`) from killing a turn at once; the 4h ceiling, four times the heaviest turn seen, bounds how long a hung worker holds its worktree's lock and a copy of an account login, and `runner.timeoutMs` above it is refused when the config loads, so the default obeys it too. The confinement reaper keeps a home whose dispatcher pid is alive and has no pane until `createdAt + max(maxAgeMs, min(marker.timeoutMs, 4h) + 10m)` (the bwrap driver records the dispatch's `timeoutMs` in the ownership marker; a marker without one keeps the 1h rule; a dead dispatcher's home goes at once, a pane-retained home is unchanged), so a pane-less run longer than an hour is no longer reaped mid-turn. The per-worktree dispatch lock (`.fgos/dispatch--.lock`, composite `pid:acquiredAtMs:rand` holder) records the `ttlMs` its holder took and keeps it across renewals; a contender judges a live composite holder by the longer of its own ttl and the holder's, so a dispatch with a shorter timeout never takes the lock of a longer run that renews only every third of its own timeout; the recorded ttl is honoured only up to the 4h ceiling. Other lock identities are judged as before. Residual: a holder killed without releasing whose pid was reused reads as live (no process start time is recorded), so it now blocks the worktree for up to its own ttl (at most 4h) instead of the contender's; `fgos dispatch reconcile` clears such a lock by hand. `--override` passed with `--resume` is ignored, as for every override key (the run keeps `unit.json#overrides`). - **RUL97 (a Unit may sync a base ref first: the runner merges it, the worker only edits the conflicted files, 2026-10-15).** A Unit may carry `syncBase` (a branch, tag or commit name: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `/`, `-`, not starting with `-` or `/`, no `..`); it needs `writes` and a linked worktree, and `fgos run --sync ` sets it (with a prompt: sync, then the task; without one: a sync-only Unit, `syncOnly: true`, whose objective is `Merge into this branch.`). The ref is resolved to a commit once, before the unit run exists (a ref naming no commit, or a run from the main checkout, leaves nothing behind), and `unit.json#sync` keeps `{ ref, sha, status, head?, conflicts?, mergeStaged?, commit? }`; a resume merges that sha, never the ref again. Before any seat runs, the runner merges it with the trusted git of RUL85 (the runner commits only the Unit's write scope) — `merge --no-commit --no-ff`, rerere and autostash off — in `src/runner/execution/commit-unit-work.mjs` (`startSyncMerge`, `finishSyncMerge`, `syncMergeState`), orchestrated by `src/runner/execution/unit-sync.mjs`: already in the branch is `up-to-date`; a clean merge is committed by the runner as `chore(sync): merge ` (status `merged`; a commit that is not the merge of `sha` over `head` holding exactly what the merge staged — a hook added a file — fails `committed-set-mismatch` as `execution-failure`, stays on the branch, and the resume is refused until a person takes it off) and the Unit goes on to its pattern, or passes at once when sync-only; a sync never brings the base side of `.fgos/` in: every `.fgos/**` path the merge staged or left conflicted, clean or not, is put back to the branch side (HEAD), a path the base deleted is kept and a path only the base has is not taken — ADR0020 (a worker branch never commits `.fgos/`), the side `fgos-write-rejected` at approve resolves to the target for a `.fgos/` path the branch left unchanged, on every branch, not only `fgw/*`; any other conflict leaves the merge open (status `conflicted`), puts the conflicted paths the scope does not already cover in scope only while the merge is open (`sync.scopeAdded`, read by the effective scope only while `sync.status === 'conflicted'`; `writeScope` itself stays as declared, so a later round cannot write them), and appends a `## Merge to finish` section to the writing seat's brief naming them and telling it never to run git. A refused start leaves no merge open and ends the run: `merge-in-progress` (a merge someone else opened), `foreign-staged-index`, `merge-refused` (git would not start, e.g. a dirty file it would overwrite), `hook-refused` (the pre-commit hook of the main checkout's hooks path refused the clean merge commit; told apart from a git failure by running that hook once more as git runs it, and its words are the detail), `unscopable-conflict-path` (a conflicted path the scope normalizer of RUL84 (one write-scope matcher) would read differently — `*`, a leading `:`, `\`, surrounding whitespace — or holding a control character, since it is also printed into the brief; the merge is aborted) as `policy-refusal`, and `git-error` as `execution-failure`. While the merge is open, the preflight of a writing seat counts only the open MERGE_HEAD equal to `sync.sha` over `sync.head` as the run's own: its conflicted and merge-staged paths are neither a foreign index nor `preExistingInScope`; any other open merge refuses a writing seat (`merge-in-progress`) and `commitUnitWork` never commits over one. After a passing round the runner concludes the merge before the round's own commit: a conflicted file that still holds a line opening with seven or more `<`, `|` or `>` (a larger `conflict-marker-size` included; a file holding a NUL byte is read as binary and not checked) fails the commit `conflict-markers` with `paths`, stages nothing and keeps the merge, so `fgos run --resume` only commits once a person removed them (RUL86 (`fgos run --resume` after a failed runner commit only commits)); otherwise it stages the conflicted paths, refuses an index holding anything the merge did not stage (`staged-set-mismatch`, taking back what it staged itself, e.g. a conflicted file the worker turned into a directory), commits with MERGE_HEAD as second parent (a refusing pre-commit hook fails it `hook-refused` with the hook's words and keeps the merge; each `fgos run --resume` tries the commit once, never in a loop), checks parents and committed set (`committed-set-mismatch`), and then commits the rest of the round inside the scope as usual. The round's `commit` carries the merge's own record under `sync`; `runUnit` returns `sync` beside `outcome`; a sync-only unit that needed no worker returns one result `{ role: 'sync', round: 0, commit }` (no `verify`, as for `solo`). A round that did not pass keeps the merge open; a resume checks it first: still open, it runs the seat again over it; concluded by hand (its sha in the branch), it is `merged`; aborted, or HEAD moved, the resume is refused and names the merge. A run that died between starting git and recording the result adopts its own open merge on resume; a first start never adopts one. A resumed sync-only run that was `up-to-date` or `merged` passes again without a worker. Settlement: the writing seat over an open merge carries `assignment.syncConflicts`; those files, dirty at launch, changed during the turn and inside its scope, count as its evidence (`evidence.editedSyncConflicts`), so a seat that only resolves conflicts is not scored `verdict-inconclusive`. Any other file dirty at launch that a seat rewrites still is no evidence, with or without a sync. A units file (`fgos workflow start --units`) naming `syncBase` is refused: a workflow unit's worktree starts from its dependency's branch, and a sync there is not built. Not done: an inline producer over an open merge (inline rounds have no runner commit), a modify/delete conflict whose worker deletes the file is concluded as a deletion. - **RUL98 (`fgos workflow start` kế thừa và phân bổ `--timeout ` và `--account ` cho từng Unit, 2026-10-15).** Workflow run hỗ trợ cờ `--timeout ` (chuỗi thời lượng hợp lệ `1m`..`4h`, phân tích ra `timeoutMs`) và `--account ` (ghim tài khoản nhà cung cấp) giống cơ chế của `--effort`. Cả hai giá trị được lưu bền vững trong payload của sự kiện `workflow.start` và được tái tạo khi `resume`. Về thứ tự ưu tiên timeout: cờ `--timeout` của `fgos run` THẮNG `unit.timeoutMs` của Unit (RUL96 (one run may take its own timeout, from 1m to 4h): override thắng unit), trong khi `--timeout` của `fgos workflow start` NHƯỜNG cho `unit.timeoutMs` tự khai của Unit. Về account: `--account` của workflow chỉ ghim cho các seat thuộc provider sở hữu account đó; các Unit không có seat nào khớp sẽ chạy bình thường không ghim và không làm hỏng workflow; `--account` không tồn tại trong bất kỳ `runner.providers.*.accounts` nào sẽ bị từ chối ngay lúc start trước khi tạo run. - **RUL99 (Bảng mã thoát riêng biệt cho kết cục thực thi của `fgos run` và `fgos workflow start|resume|answer --foreground`, 2026-10-15).** Các outcome kết thúc không phải `pass` của `fgos run` và `fgos workflow start|resume|answer --foreground` chuyển sang sử dụng bảng exit code xác định: `pass` = 0, `policy-refusal` = 4 (validation), `provider-limit` = 10, `execution-failure` = 11, `partial-writes` = 12, `blocked` = 13, `findings` = 14. Các lệnh chỉ-đọc như `fgos workflow status` luôn trả về mã thoát 0 bất kể outcome của workflow run. Lệnh `fgos workflow start` ở chế độ detached vẫn trả về mã 0 khi tiến trình daemon được khởi chạy thành công. Định dạng envelope JSON stdout `fgos.v1` giữ nguyên vẹn 100%. - **RUL100 (Doctor check `executor-posture-coverage` chẩn đoán posture readiness của các executor, 2026-10-15).** Check doctor `executor-posture-coverage` kiểm tra tĩnh khả năng áp dụng posture cho các core capabilities (`execute`, `code:implement`) và mọi capability khai báo pool agent (`prefer`). Quá trình kiểm tra chạy hoàn toàn khô qua `bind()`, không spawn tiến trình, không tạo pane herdr, không kích hoạt sandbox. Khi một capability có executor thiếu sandbox bwrap, check báo lỗi `posture-unavailable` (`passed: false`). Khi một capability thiếu pool (`headless-no-executor` / `no-candidate`), check chỉ phát cảnh báo (`passed: true`, tiền tố `warning:`) hướng dẫn khai báo `runner.capabilities..prefer`.

- **RUL77 (posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". 1. **Account lock.** One lock per provider account under `/account-locks///`, separate from the state lock, in the same append-only generation format. A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The holder records the pid of the renewal child it started: a dead holder with a live child keeps the lock, so a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are capped at five per account, the newest by staging time; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. It also stays held when the pending copies are already full and its login would only be staged, so the cap never pushes out an older copy; a staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The "trust vanishing" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself. - **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`. - **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ : }`, the key is the basename of an invocation's `command`: `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's command, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks///stores//` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each pane against the store of its own CLI. An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. Not built: per-CLI stores for an unconfined invocation, which keeps naming its store through its own env.

The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The "trust vanishing" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself. - **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`. - **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ : }`, the key is the basename of an invocation's `command`: `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's command, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks///stores//` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each pane against the store of its own CLI. An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. Not built: per-CLI stores for an unconfined invocation, which keeps naming its store through its own env.

unit.text:
- `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` — CLI (--once/--dry-run/--config/--watch/--poll-ms — str7-str8-priority-intent), exit theo phạm trù; nhánh `--watch` đăng ký `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` lên một `AbortController` chung TRƯỚC khi gọi `runWatch`, tín hiệu thứ hai buộc `process.exit(130)`; hàm `printResult` (dùng chung giữa `--once` và `onCycle` của `--watch`) nay bọc `result` (trừ `exitCode`) qua `wrapEnvelope` (`src/state/envelope.mjs`, cùng hàm `bin/fgos.mjs` dùng) và in JSON một dòng — không `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` như `fgos.mjs` — vì `--watch` phát nhiều phong bì nối tiếp theo thời gian (per str46-io-contract, xem RUL61 (kết-cục cuối của `fgos-runner` nay bọc cùng phong bì máy-đọc `fgos.v1` như mọi verb)); exit-code prose ở đầu file trỏ về `src/state/store.mjs`'s `EXIT_CODES` + `src/runner/loop.mjs`'s `EXIT_BUSY` thay vì tự liệt lại bảng
- `src/runner/loop.mjs` — vòng + startup reap (SKIP claim `human`/`session` — xem "Gặt-lại lúc khởi động") + khoá liên-tiến-trình `.fgos/runner.lock` (busy exit 6); NGAY SAU reap, TRƯỚC vòng dispatch: (1) quét mọi item `stage==='discovery' && status==='todo'` (không đọc `item.mode`), dựng worktree tạm + `spawnWorker` với `stage: 'discovery'` cho từng item, đọc khối phán quyết trong output của worker rồi gọi `resolveDiscovery` (`src/intake/discovery.mjs`) với chính verdict đó, truyền `'runner'` — nhánh không có commit nào, hoặc không đọc được verdict, thì item được để nguyên tại chỗ cho lượt sau; (2) đọc lại view tươi rồi quét mọi item ở `stageForStep(domain,'Divide')` (`planning`) CỘNG tên di sản `decompose`, với `status==='todo'`, và gọi `resolvePlan` (`src/intake/plan.mjs`) cho từng item, cùng truyền `'runner'` — không kèm verdict, nên nó chỉ cho đi thẳng khi `plan.md` của item khai mode `tiny`/`small`, còn lại no-op an toàn; cùng lượt chạy có thể chaining cả hai sweep trên một item vừa rời `discovery`; ghi bản outcome dự đoán tại claim + thực tế ở cả hai lối ra cuối (thành đề xuất, hoặc đỗ/dừng) qua `addOutcome` của store; mọi `moveWork` runner tự gọi (claim/propose/park) truyền `role:'runner'`; gọi `runGoalCheck` (từ `goal-check.mjs`, không còn tự triển khai) cho cả proof lúc dispatch lẫn proof lúc gặt-lại; ngay trước khi spawn worker, đọc lại view TƯƠI qua `listWork(dir)` rồi truyền `feedback: {answer: view.gates?.[item.id]?.answer, reason: view.work?.[item.id]?.reason}` vào `spawnWorker` (per worker-execution STR33 / 396d9d9e, xem RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker)); `dispatch.mjs` — prompt/config/spawn (argv-only, spawnSync timeout; caveat grandchild SIGTERM ghi trong doc comment) + `resolveExecutorCommand`/`resolveTierModel` (dùng chung cho mọi lượt spawn worker, kể cả lượt dispatch nghiên-cứu — không còn call site nào cho một lời gọi model phán lồng bên trong engine); `buildPrompt(work, feedback?)` dựng 5 section cố định (Goal, Description, Worktree boundary, Expected proof, Constraints — hợp đồng test pin presence) cộng mục `# Human feedback` TÙY CHỌN khi `feedback.answer`/`feedback.reason` có mặt (nguyên văn, xem RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker)); `description` là `work.description` nguyên văn, degrade "(không có)" khi vắng (per discovery-context STR30); `spawnWorker(work, cfg, cwd, opts)` nhận `opts.feedback` truyền xuống `buildPrompt`; `worktree.mjs` — lifecycle + reclaimOrphanedCheckout + `detectTrunk(repoRoot)`/`isMainWorktree(repoRoot)` (dời từ `merge.mjs` sang đây per tsk-49i — cả hai là danh tính worktree/nhánh, không mang ngữ nghĩa nội dung merge; dời đi cũng cắt luôn import vòng `merge.mjs` ↔ `worktree.mjs`) + `createBranchRef(repoRoot, id, opts)` (tạo `fgw/<id>` chỉ-là-ref, không worktree, idempotent) + `createWorktree`'s `opts.baseRef` (fork worktree mới từ một ref chỉ định thay vì HEAD hiện tại — dùng cho con fork từ tip nhánh gốc); `recovery.mjs` — 8 lớp; `anti-loop.mjs` — `visitCount` (lifetime, dùng cho outcome/metric) + `visitsSinceLastHumanEvent(events, id)` (ngân sách CỔNG, per-item, reset trên `role==='human'` mang `answer` hoặc `reason`, xem RUL29 (cổng chống-lặp reset theo can thiệp người cuối cùng của chính việc)) + breaker; `loop.mjs`'s gate (cả nhánh dry-run đơn lẻ lẫn nhánh lọc `overLimit` của batch dispatch dưới) gọi `visitsSinceLastHumanEvent`, không còn `visitCount`, để quyết park; `createMissBreaker` nay PER-ITEM (Map theo id, `consecutiveMissesFor(itemId)`; `consecutiveMisses` getter cũ giữ nguyên qua một khóa sentinel tương thích ngược, per fan-out-parallel-5). `runOnce`'s vòng dispatch nay là pool-loop batch (cell fan-out-parallel-8): đọc TOÀN BỘ `readyWork(dir)`, lọc qua `root-affinity.mjs`'s `steerFrontier`, nhóm theo gốc và cắt còn tối đa `parallel.maxRoots × parallel.maxLeavesPerRoot` (đọc từ `.fgos/config.json`'s `runner` section, mặc định 4×4 khi vắng khối `parallel`), claim từng việc bên trong callback của `write-queue.mjs`'s `enqueue` (bắt buộc — giải-và-ghi phải cùng một giao dịch hàng đợi để giữ đúng chứng minh chống-tranh-giành), rồi dispatch cả mẻ đồng thời qua `Promise.allSettled`; mỗi việc claim xong xác định LEAF hay ROOT qua `state/frontier.mjs`'s `resolveRoot(view, id)` — leaf: `createBranchRef(repoRoot, rootId, {baseRef:'main'})` rồi `createWorktree(repoRoot, item.id, {worktreeDir, baseRef: branchNameFor(rootId)})`; root: `createWorktree` không đổi, tự nhiên tái dùng nhánh đã có nếu tồn tại. Mẻ xong → đọc lại `readyWork` tươi, lặp tới khi không còn việc đang chạy VÀ không còn việc sẵn-sàng; `runOnce` trả `{outcome, dispatched, parked, reap, exitCode}` thay vì kết quả một item
- `src/runner/loop.mjs`'s `parseDiscoveredBlocks(output)` + `captureDiscoveredWork(...)` — kênh báo việc-phát-hiện (xem "Báo việc-phát-hiện từ trợ lý" trên, RUL45 (báo việc-phát-hiện của trợ lý: đúng một lần mỗi lượt, fail-safe, có trần + chống trùng)): tách mọi khối lồng `fgos-discovered` (JSON, chỉ cần `title` khác rỗng) khỏi output đã thu của trợ lý, fail-safe (thân JSON hỏng/thiếu `title`/không phải object đều bị bỏ qua, không throw); gọi đúng MỘT LẦN trong `finally` bọc vòng thử lại của `dispatchClaimedItem`, tại kết cục cuối (không gọi lại giữa các lần thử nội bộ); mỗi khối hợp lệ đi qua `write-queue.mjs`'s `enqueue` (cùng cửa ghi tuần tự) — bên trong đó: cắt còn tối đa `DISCOVERY_CAP` (=20) khối trước khi lặp (phần dư log rồi bỏ), rồi với mỗi khối: quét view hiện hành tìm item có `discoveredFrom` khớp item đang thi công VÀ tên khớp sau khi chuẩn hoá (trim + hạ chữ) — khớp thì log rồi bỏ qua (không tạo); không khớp mới gọi `generateId`/`classify`/`addWork` (đóng dấu `discoveredFrom: item.id`, và stage vào-vòng của domain — `discovery` cho `coding`); `dispatch.mjs`'s văn bản prompt worker mô tả kênh khối lồng này cho trợ lý (nguyên tắc "chỉ báo, không tự ghi" — trợ lý vẫn không bao giờ được gọi `fgos`/đụng `.fgos/`); `sanitizeTitleForLog(title)` (S11, review-fix P3) — gộp khoảng trắng/xuống dòng + cắt 120 ký tự (kèm dấu `…` khi cắt), gọi tại đúng hai điểm `log` có nội suy `block.title` bên trong `captureDiscoveredWork`; KHÔNG áp dụng lên trường `title` truyền vào `addWork`
- `src/runner/goal-check.mjs` — hàm goal-check dùng chung DUY NHẤT (`runGoalCheck(item, cwd, timeoutMs)`): chạy `item.verify` qua shell tại `cwd`, phán chỉ bằng exit status — trích xuất từ `loop.mjs` (stage-decompose S2-pull) để cả vòng tự hành LẪN cửa pull `fgos return` (spec Work-State) gọi đúng một bản logic, không bao giờ hai bản song song
- `src/runner/frozen-judge.mjs` (STR63, domain layer thuần — không fs/git) — `FROZEN_JUDGE_PATTERNS` (bê nguyên từ frozen-judge của bee, bỏ mục `.bee/config.json` không áp dụng) + `frozenJudgeHits(changedFiles, footprint)`: chấm file đã đổi khớp nhóm nhạy cảm (test/CI/lockfile/manifest) NGOÀI `footprint` đã khai — khớp exact-path, không prefix/glob. `bin/fgos.mjs`'s `changedFilesSince(cwd, from, to)` (`git diff --name-only`, cạnh `commitsSince`) cấp input; gọi trong `return` khi `check.passed`, xem RUL60 (`return` mang thêm khuyến nghị frozen-judge — advisory, không bao giờ chặn)
- `src/intake/discovery.mjs` — xem Pointers spec Work-State (module dùng chung giữa runner và verb `discover`); verb `discover` (phiên sống) truyền `'session'`; verdict đủ rõ `moveStage` tới `planning` (bỏ qua `exploring`), verdict chưa đủ rõ `moveStage` tới `exploring` RỒI đậu `awaiting-human` mang câu hỏi (hai cửa ghi rời nhau — `stage` và `status` không giẫm nhau); một đề xuất `verify` còn phải qua một vòng kiểm cú pháp độc lập trước khi được ghi, bất đồng thì cũng đậu chờ người. `judgeDiscovery` (lời gọi phán lồng cũ) đã NGHỈ HƯU: engine luôn cần một verdict do người gọi đưa vào — worker của quét nghiên-cứu, hay phiên sống gọi `fgos discover --verdict` — thiếu verdict thì role `runner` no-op an toàn, role khác báo lỗi rõ ràng
- `src/intake/plan.mjs` (đổi tên từ `decompose.mjs`) — xem Pointers spec Work-State (module dùng chung giữa runner và verb `plan` khi item ở stage `planning`, hoặc còn ở tên di sản `decompose`); verb `plan` (phiên sống) truyền `'session'`; `resolvePlan` cũng là chỗ nhả claim `doing→todo` khi gốc sang `executing` (claim-lock §3b)
- `src/runner/prompt-templates/worker-prompt-discovery.txt` — mẫu prompt riêng của lượt dispatch nghiên-cứu, chọn bởi luật `{domain:'coding', stage:'discovery'}` trong `selectTemplate` (`src/runner/prompt-templates.mjs`); mọi lời gọi không truyền `stage` giữ nguyên hành vi cũ, không bị luật này chen trước. chưa đủ rõ đẩy sang `exploring` + đậu chờ người, worker sập thì item đứng yên tại `discovery`/`todo` — cộng các kịch bản stage-clarify/stage-decompose còn lại, nay khẳng định `--once` KHÔNG tự phán ở ### 0055 — Panel: khác họ provider giữa các ghế là ưu tiên mềm, `bind()` rải ghế theo thứ tự `prefer`; `reviewed` vẫn cứng

- **Trạng thái:** Settled (owner, 2026-10-11). Thay thế quy tắc "mỗi ghế panel một họ provider khác nhau, thiếu thì từ chối" của `independentOf` cho `panel` (đặt ở abe6f2b3c, Wave B; role name resolve về executor ở 5f915db15; synthesizer bắt buộc khác họ ở 9420cf603). Phần `reviewed` (producer ≠ checker) và ngoại lệ `acceptDependence` (override `origin: human-cli`) không đổi.
- **Bối cảnh:** `panel.mjs` cho mỗi panelist `independentOf` = mọi panelist khác và cho synthesizer `independentOf` = mọi panelist; `bind()` từ chối ứng viên cùng họ trừ khi có waiver của người. Số ghế vì vậy bị chặn bởi số họ provider dùng được (5 ở máy này, đa số người dùng ít hơn) và pool thiếu họ thì synthesizer bị `policy-refusal` sau khi các panelist đã chạy và tốn tiền. Cùng họ giữa các ghế làm giảm độc lập nhưng không làm panel vô nghĩa; từ chối là hậu quả quá nặng so với lợi ích.
- **Quyết định:**
  1. **Ưu tiên mềm, không bao giờ từ chối.** `runRole` nhận thêm `preferIndependentOf` (tên vai) tách khỏi `independentOf` cứng. `panel.mjs` chỉ KHAI: mỗi panelist ưu tiên khác mọi panelist còn lại, synthesizer ưu tiên khác mọi panelist; không nêu executor/họ/tier. `independentOf` (cứng) vẫn do `reviewed` dùng.
  2. **Lựa chọn ở `bind()`, một nơi.** `ask.preferIndependentOf` là `[{ role, executor }]` của các ghế ĐÃ bind (runner/dry-bind lấy từ `role-ledger.mjs`, hàm `seats`; mảng rỗng cho ghế đầu, vắng mặt khi vai không xin rải). `bind()` vẫn lọc governance, độc lập cứng, posture, blind như cũ rồi, trong số ứng viên còn lại, chọn họ có ÍT ghế đã dùng nhất (họ chưa ai dùng = 0), hoà thì theo thứ tự `prefer` của capability (thứ tự do owner tuyển, tái dùng). Đủ họ thì ghế rơi vào họ khác nhau theo thứ tự pool như trước; hết họ thì ghế dùng chung họ ít dùng nhất. Không có bảng sức mạnh họ, bảng persona→họ, registry hay khoá config mới.
  3. **Thứ tự bind xác định.** Các panelist bind theo thứ tự liệt kê, đồng bộ trong cùng một tick (trong `runRole` không có `await` giữa `bind` và `noteRoleExecutor`), nên ghế k chỉ thấy các ghế liệt kê trước nó (cộng ghế mà lần chạy resume đã ghi); synthesizer bind sau khi mọi panelist xong. Thứ tự liệt kê = thứ tự ưu tiên: ghế đứng trước được chọn trước. Nhu cầu theo ghế (rigor/tier riêng từng ghế) chưa có kênh per-seat nên để việc sau; bước này chỉ dùng thứ tự ghế.

một danh sách candidate, người chọn đúng một hoặc dừng (Slice 1), rồi có thể
bắc cầu candidate đã chọn sang một việc thật để runner thi công (Slice 3,
`--submit`). Loop này chỉ nhắm vào chính `repo/src` của fgOS — không
phải một tính năng mở cho host project ngoài — và chạy khi người gọi tay,
không bao giờ là một nhánh tự động của vòng dispatch thường. Vòng khép
kín đầy đủ: `evolve` (liệt kê) → `evolve --pick` (xem một candidate, đọc-thuần)

PR nội bộ, với `approve` chạy thêm phán Iron Law (xem dưới) trước khi merge.

before.text:
**Quorum, retry/replacement, crash recovery, cancellation (Phase 06 R1-R4).**
Mặc định, một session chỉ đóng `completed` khi MỌI SessionActor bắt buộc đã
hoàn tất (evaluateSessionQuorum/closeSessionByQuorum,
`src/runner/coordination/session-engine.mjs`); một `partialPolicy` khai báo
NGAY LÚC MỞ session (`{minimumActors?, allowedOmissions?}`, bất biến sau đó,
không bao giờ tự chế ra lúc đóng) mới cho phép đóng `partial` — và `partial`
không bao giờ tự nhận là `completed`, trạng thái cuối luôn liệt kê đủ actor
missing/failed/late/replaced/dissenting. Retry (`retrySessionTask`) tạo một
Run MỚI cho ĐÚNG Assignment cũ (không tạo Assignment mới), theo policy
`maxRetries` khai báo; kết quả mới `supersede` view hiện hành của session
(`linkResult({allowSupersede: true})`) nhưng KHÔNG BAO GIỜ xoá/ghi đè
RunResult cũ — cả hai đều ở lại event log, bất biến. Thay actor
(`replaceSessionActor`) chỉ xảy ra qua đúng cơ chế này: bind actor mới CÙNG
role với actor cũ (không bao giờ đổi role ngầm), ghi provenance actor
cũ/mới + allocation, rồi việc dispatch thật cho actor mới vẫn đi qua đúng
`dispatchDeclaredOperation`/`dispatchPrimaryTask`/`proposeConsult` sẵn có —
không có đường dispatch tắt nào bỏ qua governance (provider/tier/diversity/
evidence). Phục hồi sau crash: mọi ghi nhiều-bước mới (retry declare ->
dispatch -> link; bind actor -> record replacement) đều tự self-heal khi
resume (không double-count, không double-dispatch), nhờ một bản ghi claim
trên đĩa riêng cho từng bước — với `replaceSessionActor`, claim khoá đúng
theo cặp (actor cũ, actor thay thế), nên một actor KHÁC đã bind sẵn vì lý
do độc lập (vd. một actor bắt buộc khai báo ngay lúc mở session nhưng chưa
từng dispatch — trạng thái MẶC ĐỊNH của một actor bắt buộc còn mới, không
phải ca hiếm) không bao giờ bị lẫn với resume của chính lệnh này và bị nuốt
mất slot bắt buộc của riêng nó; một state không rõ ràng (claim còn treo,
không rõ tiến trình cũ còn sống hay đã chết) fail closed với lỗi named rõ
hướng sửa, không bao giờ đoán liều. Cancellation
(`cancelSession`) chuyển sang trạng thái cuối `cancelled` (thêm vào
`active|completed|partial|failed`), chặn MỌI Assignment/Run mới (mọi cửa ghi
đều từ chối khi `status !== 'active'`), ghi lại ảnh chụp Assignment đang
in-flight lúc huỷ, nhưng không xoá/sửa Run/RunResult đã có; một Run in-flight
lúc huỷ vẫn được phép `linkResult` khi nó settle muộn. Mọi trạng thái cuối
(`completed|partial|failed|cancelled`) là hấp thụ — không có transition nào
đi tiếp từ trạng thái cuối. Chi tiết đầy đủ:
`docs/architect/agent-coordination/contracts/coordination-session.md`.

`plans/260915-executor-policy-dispatch-seams/design.md` — documented here so
config/doctor warnings (`executor-profile-warnings` check,
`src/setup/executor-profile-warnings.mjs`) have a named migration target to
point at. The **Invocation** half of this vocabulary was already real config
before this section existed (`executors.<id>.invocations[]`, each entry's
own `via`/`command`/`args`/`adapter` — `src/runner/dispatch/config.mjs`'s
`validateInvocationShape`). Phase C (`plans/260917-executor-profile-schema-migration/plan.md`)
made the **ExecutorProfile** half real too: `executors.<id>.identity`
(all four fields required together when declared) and `executors.<id>.supports`
(each field independently optional) are now validated, additive config
fields (`validateExecutorIdentityShape`/`validateExecutorSupportsShape`,
same file) that survive `resolveExecutorAndOverrides` unchanged. Neither
field has a real consumer yet — no resolution/dispatch/PlacementPolicy code
reads `identity`/`supports` for any decision — this is metadata a later
phase can build on, not a behavior change. `claude` is the one real
executor declaring both today (`.fgos/config.json`), proving the shape end
to end; every other `runner.executors.<id>` entry stays exactly as it was,
and legacy executor ids remain fully accepted. **No executor-id
consolidation or config-shape retirement has happened** (that is Phase E,
not started) — this section still describes the fuller target the
vocabulary is headed toward, not a completed migration.

Slice 1 hỗ trợ `openai-codex` account với `label?` và `credentialSource: { kind: "codex-home", home }`; nay mỗi account khai đúng một trong `credentialSource` (một store cho mọi CLI, kind `codex-home` hoặc `home-files`) hoặc `credentialSources` (một store cho mỗi CLI, key là tên lệnh `codex`/`pi`/`omp`/`agy`; RUL80 (account trước, CLI sau: một login store cho mỗi CLI)). Account entry bị từ chối nếu khai placement/runtime policy (`executor`, `capability`, `model`, `modelTier`, `mutation`, `confinement`, `tool`, `fallback`, `runtimeClass`, `providerRuntimes`, ...). Project-local `.fgos/config.json` bị từ chối nếu chứa `runner.providers.*.accounts`. | 6 | Trần song song hai tầng | Giới hạn số việc chạy đồng thời trong một mẻ, đọc từ cấu hình committed | tầng 1 — số việc GỐC đồng thời; tầng 2 — số việc CON đồng thời trong MỖI gốc; mỗi lần nạp mẻ lấy `min(trần, số việc sẵn-sàng sau lọc quyền-sở-hữu-gốc)` | no (có mặc định) | 4 gốc × 4 con mỗi gốc |
| 7 | Quyền sở-hữu gốc | Ai đang cầm mọi việc CON của một gốc trong MỘT lượt chạy — gắn lúc con đầu tiên của gốc được nhận, xả khi gốc xong; sống trong bộ nhớ của lượt chạy, KHÔNG bền qua lượt chạy khác/tiến trình khác | một định danh (per lượt chạy) | — | chưa-chủ |
| 8 | Bản ghi output cục bộ (một file mỗi việc) | Lưu lại output của trợ lý cho MỌI lượt dispatch của một việc — đọc được sau khi console đã cuộn qua; không bao giờ vào cây committed. Trong lúc worker chạy, file nhận con trỏ tới capture của Unit run; khối output được nối sau khi run kết thúc | mỗi khối kết-cục: dấu thời gian, số lần thử, loại kết cục (đề xuất/quá-giờ/hỏng-spawn/…), output (khi trợ lý kịp sinh ra); con trỏ Unit run được ghi khi run được tạo | no (chỉ tồn tại sau lượt dispatch đầu tiên của việc) | — |
| 9 | Candidate (Gate A, self-improve loop STR13 Slice 1) | Một việc mang ít nhất một bản ghi friction chưa ngã-ngũ, xếp hạng làm ứng viên tự cải thiện — dẫn xuất TỪ friction đã ghi, không phải một bản ghi độc lập, không bền qua lần `evolve` khác | id, disposition, errorClass, layer, detail, attempts (tất cả lấy từ bản ghi friction MỚI NHẤT theo dấu thời gian của id đó khi id có nhiều bản ghi chưa ngã-ngũ), score (cộng dồn TOÀN BỘ bản ghi chưa ngã-ngũ của id đó, không chỉ bản mới nhất) | — | dẫn xuất mỗi lần gọi `evolve` |
| 10 | Phán quyết Iron Law (self-improve loop STR13 Slice 2/3) | Kết quả của phép tính hai-cửa (module + từ khóa) trên MỘT candidate fix — dẫn xuất thuần từ đầu vào truyền vào, không bền. Gọi từ bên trong `approve` nguồn `runner` (Cổng duyệt PR nội bộ), ngay trước bước kiểm cây sạch, cho MỌI đề xuất nguồn runner đang land LÊN TRUNK (thu hẹp về ranh giới trunk per `0032`) — xem "Cổng duyệt PR nội bộ" và "Iron Law" dưới, Business Rules RUL36 (`evolve --submit` là hành động ghi duy nhất trên bề mặt evolve, tái dùng chính cửa `submit`)/RUL37 (Iron Law hỏi ở đúng một ranh giới — trunk — cho mọi đề xuất nguồn runner tới đó)/RUL64 (`ironLaw.level` — key config riêng của cổng Iron Law, fail-closed về `ask`) | required (có/không cần chứng minh test-đỏ-trước), matchedFlags (danh sách từ khóa rủi ro nặng khớp trong mô tả fix), matchedModules (danh sách file khớp danh sách module minh họa) | — | required mặc định `false` khi cả hai phép thử đều không khớp |
| 11 | Prompt template worker (STR49, `src/runner/prompt-templates/`) | Nội dung chữ nghĩa của `buildPrompt`, tách khỏi code sang file committed — sửa prompt là sửa MỘT file, không đụng code | `selectTemplate({kind, tier, domain})` — bảng luật cơ học, wildcard cuối luôn khớp (từ STR91: luật `domain: 'coding'` khớp TRƯỚC wildcard — domain vắng mặt hay không nhận diện được đều fold về `coding` giống mọi nơi khác trong hệ, không phải một fallback riêng — trỏ `worker-prompt-skill-pointer.txt`; mọi domain đã đăng ký khác `coding` (vd `synthetic`) vẫn rơi về wildcard, trỏ `worker-prompt-default.txt` như trước STR91) · `renderTemplate` — substitution `{placeholder}` string-replace thuần, không engine · `hashTemplate` — sha256 nội dung raw file, ghi kèm dispatch log (xem RUL44 (đã xây — STR49, `src/runner/prompt-templates.mjs`)) · template `worker-prompt-skill-pointer.txt` giữ đủ 6 mục cố định sẵn có, CHỈ thêm đúng một mục `# Agent skill` trỏ `SKILL.md` của domain đó — đường dẫn luôn resolve qua sổ đăng ký domain→skill (`skillForStage`, spec Work-State "Mô hình domain"), không bao giờ hardcode (xem RUL52 (luật template theo domain `coding` khớp trước wildcard; domain lạ/vắng mặt fold về `coding`)) | yes (một template mặc định luôn có) | `worker-prompt-default.txt`, `worker-prompt-skill-pointer.txt` |

before.text:
- Vòng đủ tự-cải-thiện (self-improve loop STR13): một bản ghi friction chưa ngã-ngũ mang từ khóa rủi ro nặng → `evolve` (liệt kê, candidate hiện đủ trường) → `evolve --pick` (đọc-thuần, byte-compare nhật ký trước/sau xác nhận không sự kiện nào bị thêm) → `evolve --submit` (đúng một việc mới, mô tả mang từ khóa) → runner dispatch việc mới đó tới `awaiting-approval` → `review` (source: runner) → `approve` KHÔNG `--acknowledge-iron-law` (item không cha nên target là trunk, và `ironLaw.level` mặc định `ask` — từ chối cứng, nêu tên từ khóa khớp, HEAD không đổi, nhánh còn sống) → `approve --acknowledge-iron-law` (merge, verify xanh, `awaiting-approval → done`, settlement role human, nhánh/worktree dọn sạch) — chứng minh bằng e2e qua binary + git thật, mọi bước tự chạy trong CÙNG file, không dựa vào tham chiếu chéo sang test của cell khác. Hai điều kiện trong ngoặc là điều `0032` làm thành tường minh: cùng diff ấy trên một leaf land vào `fgw/<root>`, hoặc ở `ironLaw.level = "warn"`, không dừng ở bước từ chối.
- `fgos discover <id>` gọi trên một thư mục dự án MỚI, chưa từng có cấu hình runner: không còn chết vì không đọc được cấu hình — cấu hình mặc định được tự viết tại đường mặc định, item đi tiếp vào phán làm-rõ thật (đậu `awaiting-human` khi phán không chắc, đúng fail-safe hiện có, KHÔNG phải một kết quả "thành công" trần trụi) — chứng minh bằng test thật qua binary, PATH của tiến trình phán bị thu hẹp có chủ đích để không gọi trợ lý thật nào trong lúc test. Một `--config` tường minh trỏ đường vắng mặt vẫn báo lỗi ngay như trước, không bao giờ được tự sinh thay (RUL48 (cấu hình runner tự sinh tại đường mặc định khi vắng mặt — không bao giờ đòi người tạo tay trước)).

Vòng đủ tự-cải-thiện (self-improve loop STR13): một bản ghi friction chưa ngã-ngũ mang từ khóa rủi ro nặng → `evolve` (liệt kê, candidate hiện đủ trường) → `evolve --pick` (đọc-thuần, byte-compare nhật ký trước/sau xác nhận không sự kiện nào bị thêm) → `evolve --submit` (đúng một việc mới, mô tả mang từ khóa) → runner dispatch việc mới đó tới `awaiting-approval` → `review` (source: runner) → `approve` KHÔNG `--acknowledge-iron-law` (item không cha nên target là trunk, và `ironLaw.level` mặc định `ask` — từ chối cứng, nêu tên từ khóa khớp, HEAD không đổi, nhánh còn sống) → `approve --acknowledge-iron-law` (merge, verify xanh, `awaiting-approval → done`, settlement role human, nhánh/worktree dọn sạch) — chứng minh bằng e2e qua binary + git thật, mọi bước tự chạy trong CÙNG file, không dựa vào tham chiếu chéo sang test của cell khác. Hai điều kiện trong ngoặc là điều `0032` làm thành tường minh: cùng diff ấy trên một leaf land vào `fgw/<root>`, hoặc ở `ironLaw.level = "warn"`, không dừng ở bước từ chối.
- `fgos discover <id>` gọi trên một thư mục dự án MỚI, chưa từng có cấu hình runner: không còn chết vì không đọc được cấu hình — cấu hình mặc định được tự viết tại đường mặc định, item đi tiếp vào phán làm-rõ thật (đậu `awaiting-human` khi phán không chắc, đúng fail-safe hiện có, KHÔNG phải một kết quả "thành công" trần trụi) — chứng minh bằng test thật qua binary, PATH của tiến trình phán bị thu hẹp có chủ đích để không gọi trợ lý thật nào trong lúc test. Một `--config` tường minh trỏ đường vắng mặt vẫn báo lỗi ngay như trước, không bao giờ được tự sinh thay (RUL48 (cấu hình runner tự sinh tại đường mặc định khi vắng mặt — không bao giờ đòi người tạo tay trước)).
